name: avista-activecollab
description: Run the whole task loop and the whole month-end loop in Avista's self-hosted ActiveCollab from Claude Code. Ask it what you worked on yesterday, last week, or over the billing period and it tells you which hours are on the timesheet and which are not, with the project and task each belongs to — measuring attention as a wall-clock union plus a fair-share split (the only per-project column that adds up, because directories open in the same stretch each claim that hour), folding several map entries onto one project id rather than multiplying it, and reading client email because half a day can go to correspondence that leaves no commit. The billing period resolves its start from the run log rather than arithmetic, since the nominal 19th boundary slips to whenever the cut is actually made, and offers the end as a choice instead of guessing. Per piece of work: create a task in the shape the work calls for, pull that prompt back out as a working brief, measure the hours from the git log when it lands, book them, and read them back. Per period: persist the repo-to-project mapping once, reconcile a whole window against what is logged — per project and per date, measuring from git commits and from Claude Code's own session logs (which measure attention 4x closer than commits, with no timer to remember), deduplicating shared repos cloned into every site by SHA and excluding cherry-picked older work — sweep email and calendar for billable work that left no git trace, and preflight a client before invoicing. Reconciliation is idempotent: deliberately-trashed records are read out of /trash so a deleted duplicate is never re-proposed, per-date decisions with required reasons persist last month's judgement calls, hours logged against another project count as coverage, and an append-only run log stops a half-finished posting run being repeated. The write path pre-flights budget_type — which, not is_billable, is what silently coerces billable_status to 0 — and diffs every stored field against what was sent. Includes a one-time token bootstrap that exchanges the 1Password-held login for an API token without ever storing the password, a pagination-aware API client called by full path because macOS ships its own /usr/sbin/ac that exits 0 on a wrong answer, approval-gated write skills that resolve names to IDs and read each record back to catch a silently overridden billable_status, and read-only audits that route around the time endpoints which ignore the filters they are given.
